detailed_results.question: Why do veins appear blue?
detailed_results.answer: Veins appear blue due to the way light is absorbed and scattered by skin, fat, and muscle layers. When light passes through these tissues, it is absorbed and reflected back out of the skin. The shorter wavelengths of visible light are absorbed more easily, while the longer wavelengths (red light) penetrate deeper before being reflected back out. Blue light has a shorter wavelength than red light, so it is more likely to be scattered back out of the skin, making the veins appear blue.
